newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico begins natural gas distribution rights sale.
newsitem.headline: Mexico begins natural gas distribution rights sale.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulation Commission (CRE) said on Thursday it would accept bids through January 23 on the rights to distribute natural gas in the northern state of Chihuahua.
The winning bidder, to be decided on March 20, will gain a permit to distribute natural gas in the cities of Chihuahua, Cuauhtemoc, Anahuac and Delicias.

The government, which is currently selling distribution rights to natural gas in major cities, awarded its first concession for Mexico-U.S. border city of Mexicali on August 12 to a consortium comprised of Mexican and U.S. companies.
The Chihuahua project is expected to draw $50 million in investment to the region.
Companies interested in the bidding must have five years of experience in natural gas distribution and operation systems and prove they serve at least 100,000 customers, the commission said.
The contract winner will hold exclusive distribution rights for 12 years in the region.
